target: Software engineering intern roles at quantitative trading / HFT firms (Jane Street, HRT, Citadel Securities, Optiver, IMC style), 2026–27 cycle. Score domain_fit for this domain.
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28, GPA 3.5. Leads with a C++17 IEX order book replaying 50.9M messages at 1.26M events/sec. AWS and Capital One internships.

score_rationale.concision_readability: Project bullets pack 3-4 numbers each; 686.7 ns, 1.41x mirror-only and B+/LSM ratios slow the read.
score_rationale.credibility: Latency figures need reconciling: 120 ns p50 / 1.2 us p99, 686.7 ns mean, and 1.26M ev/s (~794 ns) look inconsistent.
score_rationale.overall: Order book project is exactly what we screen for, but GPA 3.5 is below our usual bar and there are no competitive or rigor signals.

must_fix: clarify: the latency numbers across bullets 2 and 3 (p50 120 ns, p99 1.2 us, mean 686.7 ns/event, 1.26M events/sec = ~794 ns/event). Say which run and which scope (book op only vs. end-to-end with parsing/I/O) each one measures, or an interviewer will go after the gap first.
clarify: what 'full matching takes 1.41x the time of a mirror-only book' means. Most screeners won't know 'mirror-only'.

bullets.quote: Built a C++17 order book and matching engine
Indexed orders in a hash map holding iterators
bullets.issue: Strong design detail, but the latency numbers conflict with the next bullet's mean and need their run and scope stated.
bullets.suggestion: Indexed orders in a hash map of iterators into per-price FIFO queues (std::map levels) for O(1) cancels; 120 ns p50 / 1.2 µs p99 per book update on a 2M-event run

bullets.issue: 686.7 ns doesn't match 1.26M/s; the 'mirror-only' comparison is jargon.
bullets.suggestion: Sustained 1.26M events/sec end-to-end at a fixed 1.40 GHz base clock; full matching costs 1.41x a book that only mirrors the feed

bullets.quote: Traced a 1.65× phantom regression to a CPU-governor
Benchmarked B+ tree vs LSM skip-list stores
bullets.issue: Storage benchmarking is off the hot path for HFT; weakest of the five, so consider shortening it.
bullets.suggestion: Benchmarked B+ tree vs LSM skip-list stores for the event log on 2M records: B+ tree gave 12.8x read throughput for 27% more disk

bullets.quote: Writing Java policies that tune upper/lower bounds
Precomputed a tree-style search index over popular workflows
bullets.issue: Ends at intent; heavy on tool names with little low-latency relevance.
bullets.suggestion: Precomputed a tree-style search index over a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table (Redis-cached) as the Claude skill's main search tool under DB access limits

bullets.quote: Cut LLM workflow generation time 65% to
Built a Python pipeline for PhysTwin (PhD-led
bullets.issue: Off-domain for quant; dense proper nouns for a recruiter.
bullets.suggestion: Built a Python pipeline for PhysTwin (PhD-led digital twin, targeting ICLR) turning multi-camera grasp predictions into Open3D overlays for a VLM; tuned prompts for grasp choice and depth

bullets.quote: Co-founded a 110+ member campus product studio

structure.change: Keep the IEX project above Experience for this target.
structure.rationale: It is the single strongest HFT signal; leading with it is the right call.

structure.change: Keep GPA listed (omitting it reads worse at quant firms), and add relevant coursework only if it includes algorithms/OS/architecture.
structure.rationale: Firms filter on GPA; rigorous coursework can partially offset a 3.5.

structure.change: Shorten the UMIACS bullet to one line, or drop it if space is needed for project detail.
structure.rationale: ML/VLM research adds little for an HFT SWE screen and pushes systems signal down.

top3: clarify: make the order book latency/throughput figures consistent and state what each one measures (run size, scope, clock). This is the first thing a quant interviewer will probe.
clarify: replace or explain 'mirror-only book' so the 1.41x matching overhead reads at a glance.
Lighten the number density in the project bullets (shorten the B+/LSM bullet) so the three headline wins stand out: 50.9M messages exact, 1.26M ev/s, 6% to 0.06% variance.
